doc.title: J. Leo Rayhill interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 23, 2007

title: Class of musicians, Milt Hinton and jazz parties
summary: Discussion of musicians' class, dinner with Milt Hinton, and jazz parties like the Gibson.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: And you said something just a little while ago about you can’t teach that kind of class. And I’ve met an awful lot of musicians and 99 percent of them have just been, they’ve had that class. And I think it partly comes from dealing with what they have to deal with in a life of a musician, which isn’t always easy.
You had a nice one here in Milt Hinton. He was a lovely man, a lovely man. I had dinner with him and I loved him. I loved every minute I spent with him. A great guy. He loved to talk about his wife.

Uh huh. Well they were probably the most loved couple in jazz history you know. I mean they just were, you felt better when you were around them. I always used to get a kick out of watching them at the jazz parties and the festivals because they’d have this crowd, you know, everybody wanted to talk to them.
Do you ever go to those jazz parties?
No I never did. The one out west I understand was the best.
Yeah the Gibson. I got some tapes of the party and I got some records.
They do one in Chautauqua now.
